item.title: How does eastern Europe commemorate the Roma Holocaust?
item.description: In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: War in Ukraine: Why Crimea has become a strategic target
item.description: Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian logistics centers and energy facilities in Crimea. What are the consequences for local supplies, and how does Kyiv hope this strategy will affect the course of the war?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: How crypto miners are stealing power in Southeast Asia
item.description: Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids, and exposing links to organized crime.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Sudan civil war: When drones strike the classroom
item.description: Children in Sudan's besieged city of el-Obeid are afraid to go to school as drone attacks hit civilian infrastructure. Aid groups warn of a worsening humanitarian crisis.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
item.description: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominates. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

item.title: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
item.description: Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India's 'Cockroach' protesters face ongoing legal pressure
item.description: After forcing the resignation of India's education minister, student activists say a crackdown continues despite government promises to drop criminal cases against protesters.

item.title: Military flare-up between Houthis and Saudi Arabia challenges relative calm in Yemen
item.description: Riyadh and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are on the brink of renewed conflict. Could war-ravaged Yemen be drawn into a wider Middle East war?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Spain's PM visits Ceuta after thousands breached border
item.description: Thousands of people continued pouring into Ceuta from Morocco during the night, after Spanish police lost control of the border. The head of the city government estimated that 60,000 people had entered.

item.title: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
item.description: US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.
